Write the JSON input file for a TreePPL model

Source: R/data.R
tp_data.Rd

tp_data() writes the R objects in data to a JSON file that a TreePPL sampler can read, and checks the file against the model's arguments. Pass the result to tp_run().

Usage

tp_data(model, data, filename = NULL, check = TRUE, print = TRUE)

Arguments

model

Name of a model in the TreePPL model library (see tp_model_library()), e.g. "crbd", or the path to a .tppl model file.

data

A named list with one element per model argument.

filename

Path of the JSON file to write. If NULL (default), the file is written to tp_tempdir() and named after the model and a hash of data, so the same data always gets the same file name and different data a different one.

check

Logical. If TRUE (default), check the written file against the model with tp_input_check() and print the result.

print

Logical. If TRUE (default), print a summary of the input file: its path, the model and the arguments it expects.

Value

Invisibly, a list of class tpData with elements:

  • data_path: path to the JSON file.

  • model_name: the model's name.

  • expect_args: the model's argument names, in signature order.

  • expect_types: the TreePPL type of each argument.

  • expect_class: the R object expected for each argument.

Typing the object at the console prints its summary again (see print.tpData()).

Details

Each element of data must be named exactly like an argument of the model; the order does not matter. Use tp_expected_input() to see the names and the R object each argument expects.

Trees must be given as tpPhylo objects, built from a phylo tree with tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo(). A phylo object in data is not converted automatically and stops tp_data() with an error.

The file is written with the settings TreePPL needs: values of length 1 become plain JSON values, numbers keep full precision, and matrices are written row by row.

See also

tp_expected_input() for the arguments a model expects, tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo() to build trees, tp_run() to run a sampler on the file.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
phy <- ape::read.tree(text = "((A:4,B:4):6,(C:7,D:7):3);")

# Diversification model: a tree and the sampling fraction
d <- tp_data(
  model = "crbd",
  data = list(tree = tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo(phy), rho = 0.5)
)
d            # prints the summary again
d$data_path  # path to the JSON file

# Write to a chosen file, without the check or the summary
d <- tp_data(
  model = "crbd",
  data = list(tree = tp_phylo_to_tpPhylo(phy), rho = 0.5),
  filename = "crbd_input.json",
  check = FALSE,
  print = FALSE
)
} # }
